summary: The single mismatch is Linux/Darwin build provenance at step 10: Unix versus MacOS and /dev/urandom versus /dev/random. All 4251 RNG calls and 33 cursors match. The v32 manifest explicitly excludes these bytes from portable game behavior; retain canonical Darwin output and park this platform boundary without a source implementation claim.

source.branch: The #version command enters doextversion on the Unix/Linux recorder build. getversionstring reads version_id assembled with compile-time PORT_ID, while runtime option text includes compile-time DEV_RANDOM. JavaScript deliberately uses the Darwin judge build profile.
callers: allmain.c:moveloop_core -> cmd.c:rhack -> cmd.c:doextcmd -> version.c:doextversion (cmd.c:1924–1925 registration; js/cmd.js:5225–5230 awaited dispatch)
pager.c:hmenu_doextversion:2790–2793 -> version.c:doextversion (js/pager.js:2258), the independently validated help-menu entry
dependencies: mdlib.c:version_id_string:316–344 consumes compile-time PORT_ID; global.h:184–222 selects MacOS for __APPLE__ and otherwise Unix for UNIX.
mdlib.c:build_options:669–826 consumes build_opts and opt_out_words; build_opts:511–514 includes DEV_RANDOM; unixconf.h:419–430 selects /dev/urandom under LINUX and /dev/random under BSD/MACOS.
No missing consumed-return gameplay callee or input dependency was observed. The blocker is the established build-profile compatibility contract, not an unported source function.

evidence: Current authoritative accepted-B178 evaluation at 6f43faf156d28688e1e9bf2470077de98e6cc4b2 reports 32/33 screens, 4251/4251 RNG and 33/33 cursors. Assigned-session-only replay at worker commit 8bff1f85c1609befc42edbdb85b7f882e38c9965 reproduces exactly those totals, with no runtime refusal or input boundary. Receipt: /tmp/teleport-validation-1000/run-W4F8Db/receipt.json; diagnostic: .cache/A178/replay.json.

The first differing byte is segment 0, zero-based step 10, row 0 column 0, after the newline completing #version: C prints Unix NetHack Version 5.0.0 - last build May  2 2026 12:00:00.; JS prints the same release/build clock with MacOS. The only other differing row is row 8, where the seed-device label is /dev/urandom in C and /dev/random in JS. All other 32 screens, all RNG, cursors and zero animation frames match.

version.c:getversionstring:35–81 copies nomakedefs.version_id. mdlib.c:version_id_string:316–344 formats PORT_ID with the numeric release and pinned build date. global.h:184–222 defines the platform identity from compiler configuration. js/version.js:16–17 and getversionstring:109–111 intentionally preserve the canonical Darwin identity. The deterministic-runtime patch pins the date, not PORT_ID.

version.c:doextversion:169–276 builds the text window in source order. Its row-8 option data comes from mdlib.c:runtime_info_init -> build_options -> opt_out_words, using the DEV_RANDOM member of build_opts at mdlib.c:511–514. unixconf.h:419–430 explains the Linux/Darwin device difference. js/mdlib.js:25 selects the canonical /dev/random phrase; no RNG operation reads this informational label.

The admitted v32 manifest case sourceTrace explicitly identifies the same two differences as platform/build-data provenance, not a new portable game behavior. Its independent C replay reproduced the same bytes. The manifest retains the case as an uncounted configuration/startup frontier.

scripts/run-help-version-information.mjs:3–25 and scripts/fresh-matrix.mjs:14–45 document the existing compatibility rule: keep Darwin judge strings in game code and normalize only these two compile-time host strings for qualified fresh comparisons. Raw synthetic scoring remains strict. Replacing the JS literals with Linux text would contradict that established contract and threaten Darwin recordings.

No portable source implementation task is justified by this case. If the project later changes its build-profile contract, the bounded affected owners are version.c:getversionstring/mdlib.c:version_id_string and mdlib.c:build_options, with both direct #version and help-menu callers already wired. Independent validation must cover both entry points, exact pagination/RNG/cursors and the two profiles; session/seed detection or expected-screen branching is invalid. No game code, tests, recipes, recordings, evaluations or manifest were changed in this investigation.

resolution.reason: The Linux C recorder embeds Unix and /dev/urandom while the JavaScript port preserves the Darwin judge profile, MacOS and /dev/random. The manifest classifies those compile-time labels as platform/build-data provenance rather than portable game behavior.
resolution.disposition: Retain the Darwin judge profile and preserve the admitted v32 recording, manifest, and evaluations unchanged. Exclude this platform-only mismatch from JavaScript implementation work.
